speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy having trouble feeding and feeling bloated; have you noticed any vomiting, especially if it is green or foul-smelling, or if your belly looks unusually tight?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: Since touching the belly makes him cry and he is refusing food, have you noticed any visible wave-like movements in his stomach, or has he passed any gas or stool recently? Please check if his abdomen feels hard like a board or if you can see veins bulging under the skin. Also, please tell me if he has been passing gas at all.

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for the history. Since there is no vomiting or stool passed, and the abdomen is tender to touch, have you noticed any swelling in the scrotum or a bulge coming from the groin area that might suggest a hernia? Also, can you tell me if he has been passing gas at all?

REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_Ultrasound, Scrotal_Ultrasound

speaker: Patient
text: The baby did not seem to pass stool normally and the belly swelling has become more obvious. Feeding has clearly decreased over the past few days.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Intussusception. The clinical picture of an 8-month-old male presenting with progressive abdominal distension, feeding refusal, abdominal tenderness, and a history of interrupted stool passage without fever or vomiting is highly suggestive of intussusception. The absence of a hernia bulge makes this more specific to internal telescoping of the bowel. I have requested the Abdominal and Scrotal Ultrasound to confirm the presence of the pathognomonic "target sign" or "doughnut sign" in the abdomen and rule out incarcerated inguinal hernia. If the ultrasound confirms the diagnosis, immediate surgical consultation and potential air enema reduction are required.
